captions.instagram:
How does a cloudburst happen?

No cloud ever bursts. A cloudburst is a storm whose rising air holds tens of thousands of tonnes of water in the sky and then lets it fall on one small valley: 100 mm in an hour. Fill a rain gauge, hold water aloft and drop it, push monsoon wind up a Himalayan slope, watch a stream become a torrent in minutes, and learn why the only safe move is uphill.

→ A cloudburst is 100 mm of rain in one hour, on a patch only a few kilometres wide.
→ That is 100 litres on every square metre. A drizzle would need four days to match it.
→ No cloud bursts like a bag. Fast rising air holds tens of thousands of tonnes of water in the sky.
→ When the updraft weakens, the water it was holding falls together, in minutes, on one small place.
→ Mountains make them: moist monsoon wind is forced up a steep slope, and the valley holds the storm in place.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/cloudburstclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a cloudburst happen? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
No cloud ever bursts. A cloudburst is a storm whose rising air holds tens of thousands of tonnes of water in the sky and then lets it fall on one small valley: 100 mm in an hour. Fill a rain gauge, hold water aloft and drop it, push monsoon wind up a Himalayan slope, watch a stream become a torrent in minutes, and learn why the only safe move is uphill.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/cloudburstclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/cloudburstclear

In this video:
• An hour of rain like a month. The India Meteorological Department calls it a cloudburst when a place gets 100 mm of rain or more in one hour.
• No cloud bursts. A cloud is not a bag of water.
• Why mountains make them. Rain at one place is the rate times how long it lasts.
• From sky to stream. Thin soil soaks up perhaps 15 mm an hour.
• Hard to see coming. A cloudburst is a few kilometres wide and over within the hour.
• India, and staying safe. Leh 2010, Kedarnath 2013, Amarnath 2022, Himachal Pradesh 2023, Dharali and Chashoti 2025: the storms are old, but more roads, hotels and camps now stand in stream beds and on fans.
